--- title: "ETV Cycle 01 — Coffee Spending" subtitle: "STAT/DATA 1810 · In-class activity · SOLUTION" author: "Instructor key" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 toc-location: right-body toc-title: "Contents" execute: warning: false message: false --- ::: {.callout-warning title="Timing & CLOs"} - **Budget:** Ethics 8′ · E 12′ · T 30′ · V 20′ · Answer 10′ = **80′** - **CLOs:** 2.1 `read_csv` · 3.1 select/filter/mutate/summarize · 4.1 ggplot + `geom_point` · 4.4 center & spread · 4.5 claim · 12.4 privacy ::: # 0 · Context & ethics [8 min]{.timing} ::: {.callout-important title="Talking points (CLO 12.4)"} - Our data: **821 entries** from a personal transaction ledger - Transaction logs can reveal routines, locations, and financial habits - Model sentence: *"Someone might not expect a personal ledger to be used to infer their routine or financial situation."* ::: # 1 · The central question > **How much do customers spend on coffee, and how does the amount spent vary?** # 2 · E — Extraction [12 min]{.timing} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) # LM1: import the data coffee_df <- read_csv("Data/coffee_purchases.csv") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM2: inspect glimpse(coffee_df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 821 Columns: 7 $ date 17826, 17833, 18050, 18057, 18136, 18176, 18271, 18274, 18… $ description "SQ *LUCY'S COFFEE C 10/21 PURCHASE SAN LUIS OBIS CA", "SQ… $ amount -20.10, -7.43, -2.75, -2.75, -9.21, -5.33, -12.91, -2.75, … $ account "Kelley", "Eman", "Eman", "Eman", "Kelley", "Eman", "Eman"… $ month "October", "October", "June", "June", "August", "October",… $ year 2018, 2018, 2019, 2019, 2019, 2019, 2020, 2020, 2020, 2020… $ day_of_week "Monday", "Monday", "Monday", "Monday", "Wednesday", "Mond… ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Expected — LM2"} - [LM2]{.lm} **821 rows, 7 variables** - `amount` (``) stores debits as **negative** dollar values - `description`, `account`, `month`, `year` provide the available context ::: # 3 · T — Transformation [30 min]{.timing} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM3: select the relevant variables coffee_small_df <- coffee_df |> select(description, amount, account, month, year) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM4: keep coffee purchases with recorded debits coffee_clean_df <- coffee_small_df |> filter(str_detect(description, regex("coffee", ignore_case = TRUE)), !is.na(amount)) nrow(coffee_small_df) - nrow(coffee_clean_df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 77 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Expected — LM4"} - [LM4]{.lm} **77 rows removed**, leaving **744** coffee descriptions - Defense clause students should produce: *"The description is our operational rule for identifying coffee, but it may miss or include some purchases."* - The negative sign is expected — the source is a transaction ledger ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM5: convert ledger debits to positive spending coffee_clean_df <- coffee_clean_df |> mutate(spending = -amount) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM6: center and spread spending_summary_df <- coffee_clean_df |> summarize( mean_spending = mean(spending), sd_spending = sd(spending), n = n() ) spending_summary_df ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Expected — LM6"} - [LM6]{.lm} mean ≈ **$5.95** · sd ≈ **$5.45** · n = **744** - The large spread is partly driven by unusually large ledger entries — interpret, don't memorize ::: # 4 · V — Visualization & summary [20 min]{.timing} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM7: histogram of spending ggplot(coffee_clean_df, aes(x = spending)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, fill = "#12263A", color = "white") + labs(x = "Coffee spending ($)", y = "Purchases", title = "Coffee spending varies across ledger entries") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etv01_coffee_solution_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM8: geom_point — every purchase visible ggplot(coffee_clean_df, aes(x = account, y = spending)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "#12263A") + labs(x = "Account", y = "Coffee spending ($)", title = "Coffee spending by account — one point per purchase") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etv01_coffee_solution_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: *(Optional boxplot, if the class is ahead:)* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(coffee_clean_df, aes(x = account, y = spending)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "#E3C36F") + labs(x = "Account", y = "Coffee spending ($)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etv01_coffee_solution_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important title="Teaching note — LM8"} - [LM8]{.lm} Points show the full transaction-level spread that the summary table compresses away - The account groups make the limits of the dataset visible: this is a **ledger, not a random sample** of all customers ::: # 5 · Interpretation & final answer [10 min]{.timing} ::: {.callout-tip title="Model answer"} - *"A typical recorded coffee purchase is about $5.95, with a standard deviation of roughly $5.45. The plot shows that the ledger contains many small purchases and a few much larger entries. We retained 744 of 821 rows whose descriptions contained 'coffee'; that text rule is useful but not perfect."* - Required elements (the CLO 4.5 rubric for every cycle this term): - **center** — the mean - **spread** — the sd, in dollars - **caveat** — the filter rule :::
